The title is fake. Tenerife doesn´t have gold, gemstones, rare earths, gas or anything ike that. We have an amazing weather but for the rest of it....seawage waters thrown at the shore without a propper treatment, traffic congestion because the overload of cars , the impossibility to enjoy our beaches or even to go to El Teide without the ridiculous amount of people everywhere, even the neighbours of remote areas like Anaga have to deal with an oversaturation of cars and people of what is a tiny road, if someone needs to get evacuated by ambulance is going to be done even before the ambulance gets to them.... 
Also, you have Islands like greenland, New Zealand, Madagascar, Taiwan....which are waaaaaay richer....So the title is a lie

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: Tenerife is fascinating because you have an active volcano, dramatic mountains, black-sand beaches, and beautiful coastal towns all on one island. It's incredible how nature has shaped both the landscape and the way people live here. What a remarkable place.

comments.author: @MrCuriousEN
comments.text: Tenerife is a perfect example of how tourism can create both prosperity and pressure at the same time. 🌋🏝 Millions of visitors support jobs and businesses, yet limited land, housing demand and water scarcity make island life increasingly complicated for residents. The volcanic landscape is spectacular, but the social geography behind the postcard is probably the more important story.

comments.author: @WorldsOffTheMap
comments.text: Tenerife is such a fascinating island! Between the beautiful beaches, the charming streets of La Laguna, and the incredible views around Mount Teide, there's so much to explore. I wonder what it's like to live here and enjoy these views as part of everyday life!

comments.text: It's crazy how a place can be paradise for tourists while locals struggle to afford a home. Anyone from Tenerife know how bad the housing situation really is?💥
